subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The Four Forces of Flight
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Four Forces of Flight.

hook.text: Every aircraft in flight is balanced between four forces: lift, weight, thrust, and drag. Change one, change everything.

buildup.text: Lift opposes weight. Thrust opposes drag. In straight, level flight, all four are in equilibrium.

discovery.text: Drag increases with the square of speed — double your speed and drag quadruples. This limits how fast planes can fly efficiently.

twist.text: At the speed of sound, drag spikes dramatically. This 'sound barrier' stopped aviation for years until Chuck Yeager broke it.

climax.text: Modern aircraft are shaped to minimize drag while maximizing lift. Every surface is optimized down to the rivet pattern.

punchline.text: Four forces. One balance. The physics of everything that flies.

quiz.question: What happens to aerodynamic drag when an aircraft doubles its speed?
options: Drag doubles proportionally with the increase in speed
Drag quadruples because it increases with the square of speed
Drag stays the same until the aircraft reaches the speed of sound
